items.title: XBOX Game Pass Brings Bad News for Cyberpunk 2077 Fans
items.content:
XBOX Game Pass Brings Bad News for Cyberpunk 2077 Fans From DualShockers (Written by Jake Valentine) on September 1, 2026 | OpenCritic

Good news: we're getting seven new games on XBOX Game Pass to start September off.

Bad news: it comes at the cost of some great titles.

In total, 10 games will be leaving the Game Pass library on September 15th, including some heavy hitters.

This is the second time in a month a major CD Projekt RED RPG has left Game Pass. The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Complete Edition left the service on August 31st, 2026. It's unclear whether or not the upcoming Witcher 3 Remaster will be available when it launches.

Obviously, the big-ticket item here is Cyberpunk 2077, but there's also the added value of games like Dead Cells, Spiritfarer, and Deep Rock Galactic Survivor that will no longer be part of Game Pass moving forward.

It all adds up to some pretty big losses for one of XBOX's flagship services, especially when you account for the negative press it and the company as a whole have received over the past twelve months.

Last October, Microsoft increased the cost of a Game Pass Ultimate subscription by 50%. It was a move that, according to XBOX founder Laura...

items.title: Game Pass Ultimate Gets Off To A Slow Start In September 2026
items.summary: Cyberpunk 2077 departs with not much to take its place
items.content:
Xbox has revealed the first batch of new games for September 2026, and it’s a bit thin. On top of there being only one new game exclusive to the Game Pass Ultimate tier in the last weeks of summer, heavy hitters like Cyberpunk 2077 are leaving halfway through the month.

The Game Pass headliner for the first half of September is Speedrunners 2: King of Speed , a multiplayer 2D platforming racer that’s a sequel to a 2016 game that remains highly reviewed on Steam. That’s definitely neat, but it’s also the only upcoming addition that won’t also be coming to the cheaper Game Pass Premium tier, suggesting that Ultimate subscribers aren’t necessarily getting their money’s worth at the moment.

Here’s everything joining Xbox Game Pass in wave 1 for September 2026 :

Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War and Virtua Fighter 5 R.E.V.O. World Stage are other notable additions, but both are quite old. Elsewhere, Xbox notes that TCG Card Shop Simulator , which is already on the service, is getting its 1.0 release on September 15, while EA Sports NHL 27 will get an early access trial starting September 4. Plus, people lining up to play Aniimo , the new Pokémon -like RPG with questionable AI use, will get a free reward pack to kick off their journeys.

Unfortunately, Cyberpunk 2077 isn’t the only big game leaving on September 15. Dead Cells , Deep Rock Galactic Survivor , Frostpunk 2 , Mullet Madjack , and Spiritfarer are all out the door too. Subscribers can’t complain too much—August was an exceptional month for the service—but hopefully the second half of September picks up for Game Pass Ultimate. It would be a shame if the next month ended up feeling like filler before Gears of War: E-Day stomps onto the scene in October.

items.title: CD Projekt Red "Very Happy" With Cyberpunk 2077 Sales On Switch 2
items.summary: "the most important bit is that the players are happy"
items.content:
"the most important bit is that the players are happy"

It's safe to say that, besides from Mario Kart World , CD Projekt Red's Cyberpunk 2077: Ultimate Edition was the game of the Switch 2's launch in 2025.

That probably sounds strange considering it's a port of a title that infamously had a disastrous start on other platforms, but by the time it released on Nintendo's new console, it has been improved significantly and was widely considered one of the most impressive open-world games available.

So it's no surprise that it sold well, but according to CEO Michał Nowakowski in an interview with The Game Business, CD Projekt Red was "very happy" with Cyberpunk's commercial performance on Switch 2. Because its launch aligned with the console's, the team didn't know what to expect, but it was apparently the best-selling third-party game "for a while", even surpassing some of Nintendo's first-party offerings.

“We were the best-selling third-party game on Switch 2 for a while, I think, when we launched. In fact, we were overselling quite a few Nintendo games – their own games – with the exception of course Mario Kart.

"I think that was a success on its own. We were very happy by the way, with the sales numbers on the platform. Made money on it, broke even. We’re in the positive. It is a peculiar platform because it’s, you know, it was at its launch moment, so the install base was not as huge, so we never expected numbers of, I don’t know, Steam or something like that.

"But we did very well. And actually the game continues to sell. We’re happy. And the most important bit is that the players are happy. I believe Nintendo was very happy as well. Everything we heard from them was praised. They were also very impressed with how the game performed on the hardware – the special features of Cyberpunk on Switch 2 and so on, so wait and see for The Witcher now.

"This was a bit of a test for us because this was literally the first time ever for us to be on the platform at launch, so we kind of didn’t know what to expect. But we liked the hardware so much and the pitch that Nintendo had overall for the whole ecosystem that we decided to give it a shot. And I think it paid off. We’re happy.”

We're happy that the game seems to be doing well for CD Projekt Red, and it's clear from overall reception that the team successfully managed to reverse its fortunes after such a poor launch back in 2020. We gave it a score of 9/10 in our review, stating "Its deep, diverse, and tangible world is fully realised with impressive performance for such a low-powered device".

items.title: Xbox Game Pass Removes Cyberpunk 2077 And 9 Other Games Very Soon
The Witcher 4 Dev Reveals How It Won’t Repeat Cyberpunk 2077’s Mistakes
items.summary: CD Projekt Red is well aware of its missteps with Cyberpunk 2077 and has changed its development process with The Witcher 4.
items.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook While Cyberpunk 2077 has gone on to be one of the most beloved RPGs of the past decade, this wasn’t the case at launch. Upon its arrival in 2020, Cyberpunk 2077 was littered with bugs, performance struggles, and a host of additional issues that made many feel like the game was released too early. This controversy resulted in developer CD Projekt Red taking a rather major hit to its reputation, which has somewhat continued to loom over the studio. Now, with CDPR gearing up to release The Witcher 4 in the coming years, the team behind the much-anticipated sequel has opened up about how it’s not repeating the same mistakes as before.

Speaking to Game Developer , CD Projekt Red’s co-CEO Michal Nowakowski said that the company has ensured that The Witcher 4 can internally run on both consoles and PCs right now. Throughout its development on Cyberpunk 2077 , Nowakowski explained that the studio focused too heavily on the PC version, as it thought it could easily adapt this edition to consoles later on. As it turned out, this ended up presenting a lot of problems with Cyberpunk 2077 across Xbox and PlayStation hardware, which is why these versions of the game ended up being in a worse state upon their release. For The Witcher 4 , CD Projekt Red has abandoned this development process, as it’s now developing all versions of the game at once and making sure that they can run well in advance of launch.

“The way the studio was thinking was that we are reaching for the best possible visuals,” Nowakowski said of Cyberpunk 2077’s development. “We want to push the boundaries of what is doable in terms of cinematic feeling and whatnot, and PC was just the best suited rig for that. There was this, as it turned out, false belief that toning it down to whatever was the current gen is not going to be that much of a challenge. […] Since then, we don’t take chances. We want to be sure that it actually works.”

Beyond putting a greater focus on the console versions of The Witcher 4 , Nowakowski said that it has also made sure that any issues that pop up with the game are addressed almost immediately. In the past, Nowakowski mentioned that CDPR would occasionally push certain problems down the road, which would lead to them building up and presenting greater issues. Now, this is something that those within the studio have stopped doing, which should make The Witcher 4 much less buggy by the time it does arrive.

Speaking of which, CD Projekt Red recently confirmed that The Witcher 4 is targeting a release in 2028. In the interim, though, the studio will be releasing a new remaster of The Witcher 3 at the end of this month , which will precede the game’s new Songs of the Past expansion, which launches in 2027.

items.title: CD Projekt Red: If you want a cost-driven development, you cannot make The Witcher 4
items.summary: Joint CEO Michał Nowakowski on making multiple projects, the console market, and returning to The Witcher 3
items.content:
Playback speed × Share post Share post at current time Share from 0:00 0:00 / Generate transcript A transcript unlocks clips, previews, and editing. 9 1 CD Projekt Red: If you want a cost-driven development, you cannot make The Witcher 4 Joint CEO Michał Nowakowski on making multiple projects, the console market, and returning to The Witcher 3 Christopher Dring Sep 01, 2026 9 1 Share Transcript Listen now on Apple , Spotify or YouTube In This Edition, CD Projekt Red joint CEO Michał Nowakowski on…

Plus, discs, Unreal Engine, Switch 2, TV shows, and more

Death is the great motivator. And it’s certainly motivating CD Projekt Red.

For 20 years, The Witcher developer has worked on one major project at a time. But today, it’s making three. There’s The Witcher 4, due in 2028, a sequel to Cyberpunk and a new IP called Project Hadar.

“Everybody has a biology built into them. We were like, ‘if we keep doing things the way we do, and we have a lot of ideas, we’re only going to make X, Y, Z before we retire, or naturally retire from this place’,” says CD Projekt Red joint CEO Michał Nowakowski on today’s The Game Business Show .

“So how can we do more, but not compromise on quality? This was the predominant thought behind that. And then we started thinking, ‘Okay, what’s the business around that?’ This is my biggest wish. I’d like us to look back and say, ‘Okay, we did it, we told two, three stories instead of just one within that moment, and all of them were top-notch’.”

The cynic might suggest that there’s another, more commercial reason why CD Projekt Red would want to develop multiple major games at once. But Nowakowski believes financial growth isn’t entirely down to making more games. The Witcher 3 may now be on 65 million sales, with Cyberpunk 2077 on 40 million, but there’s room to sell more, he says.

“If you look at what GTA V sold, these are very different numbers to what we have achieved. There is still room for growth.”

There is another option to getting more games out, and that’s to simply make them faster. Not only would that allow CD Projekt Red to release more, it’d also help bring down costs. But it’s not how the studio thinks.

“We are cost-conscious,” Nowakowski explains. “It’s not unimportant. We’re a business in the end. But the first thing is whether the qualityis there, period. This is the dominant thing we look at.

“I definitely wouldn’t put cost in the number one position, as weird as that may sound. We try to make sure we’re within the boundaries, or if it’s exceeding, then we sit down and think what it means for everything. But I definitely wouldn’t say this is a cost-driven development. If you want to have a cost-driven development, and that’s a proper business thinking for a lot of games, you cannot make a game like The Witcher 4. I doubt if the development of GTA VI was a cost-driven development. In fact, I’m 100% sure it wasn’t.”

Nevertheless, to achieve the goal of multiple projects does require a technical rethink. The developer has walked away from its REDengine, which powered The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077, in favour of Unreal Engine. Nowakowski tells us that REDengine needed starting from scratch with each new release. By moving to Unreal, it should make switching between projects simpler.

Initially, there will be some pain. Pipelines and tools will need reworking and changing. But the bigger threat from this technical pivot is whether using an off-the-shelf engine might negatively impact the uniqueness of the games.

“That was a big question we were asking ourselves, because pushing the envelope with how the games look, the cinematic feel of it all, is very, very important,” Nowakowski answers. “And that was a big question mark when we were in the R&D phase over whether Unreal Engine 5 is going to be a good fit or not. We really asked ourselves all of these questions, and in some cases the answer was, ‘not yet.’

items.title: After the debacle of Cyberpunk 2077, CD Projekt says The Witcher 4 is already running on PC and consoles, promises 'it's going to run' on all target platforms
items.content:
Sure, it's a low bar, but after the Cyberpunk 2077 fiasco you can understand why CD Projekt Red would want to make the point.

But Cyberpunk 2077 then , which is to say when it was new, was not. It was pretty okay on PC , aside from a horde of bugs, but it was such a performance catastrophe on the PlayStation 4 that Sony literally booted it off the PlayStation Store . Even when it was allowed back in the building six months later, Sony slapped a notice on it warning people that it was still potentially dodgy .

Speaking to Game Developer , CD Projekt Red co-CEO Michał Nowakowski said that failure arose from the studio's ambitions for the game, which led it to develop on PC first. "We want[ed] to push the boundaries of what is doable in terms of cinematic feeling and whatnot [in Cyberpunk 2077], and PC was just the best suited rig for that," Nowakowski said. "There was this, as it turned out, false belief that toning it down to whatever was the current gen is not going to be that much of a challenge."

There was also a little bit of belief in a Polish take on the ol' Bioware magic : Nowakowski said the studio "got a bit lucky here and there" with The Witcher 3 , leading it to believe that Cyberpunk would ultimately be fine too.

Of course, Cyberpunk 2077 was most definitely not fine, and with that humiliation firmly burned into its collective consciousness, CD Projekt Red is approaching The Witcher 4 with a little more care and consideration to ensure the new game runs properly on all platforms it's coming to. If development hits a snag on any single platform, for instance, the studio stops to fix it rather than simply pressing ahead and coming back to clean it up later.

"For example, technically, we should hit, let's say, 10 checkmarks," Nowakowski said. "Back in the past, if we missed one or two, we were like, 'we're gonna catch up with that later on.' Sometimes we did, but sometimes we didn't, and then two milestones or three milestones down the road, you have like four or five missing checkmarks and it's not that easy."

CD Projekt Red boss believes some fans were forever burned by Cyberpunk 2077's disastrous launch: 'I'm convinced that we lost the faith of some people indefinitely' Cyberpunk 2077 has now sold more than 40 million copies, 'a testament to what CD Projekt does best' The Witcher 4 is 'targeting' a 2028 release The net result is parity right from the get-go: "You come to the studio, you launch Witcher 4 right now. You can launch it on PC. You can launch it on PS5. You can launch it on Xbox Series X, and it's going to run," Nowakowski said.

'We're doing our best to ensure our game runs' is a low bar, sure, but given how poorly Cyberpunk 2077 went at launch it's not surprising that CD Projekt is making the point—and so, here's hoping it's able to pull it off. The Witcher 4 still doesn't have a release date (and probably won't for a good long time yet) but is currently "targeting" a 2028 release .

Mimic developer Ryan Laley said on Friday that "all our laptops have been stolen," ending his team's event presence early. Amidst the wave of support his message sparked, Cyberpunk 2077 and The Witcher 3 developer CD Projekt Red reached out to hopefully help replace the lost hardware.

"We are very sorry this happened to you," a reply from the Cyberpunk 2077 Twitter account reads. "We hope you know you're not on your own with this. And while it won't help right this second, we'll check the Arasaka hardware archives and see if we can send a few things your way. No choom should have to start from zero."

The official account for Where Winds Meet, a wuxia action RPG from Everstone Studios and Netease Games, also offered support: "We're so sorry this happened to you. We hope you know you're not on your own. Wanderers are here to help. We'll stop by your booth tomorrow with what we can and do our part to help get you back in the game."

At least three teams have reported stolen Gamescom equipment this year. One impacted team, Ukiyo Studios, said on Sunday, "We had an Xbox controller, drinks and food stolen from our booth today. The drinks and food were stolen overnight, and the controller was taken around 18:50. This makes it 4 years straight of things being stolen. This is the cost of doing business in Gamescom."

Gamescom organizers have now addressed the latest robberies. In an August 29 statement, the event's official account said, "We are aware of stolen hardware and take these reports very seriously and understand the frustration of affected exhibitors."

Cyberpunk 2077 was a lesson for CD Projekt Red. After its disastrous launch and subsequent removal from the PlayStation Store, developer CD Projekt Red now makes sure that its games are working on all platforms throughout development, co-CEO Michal Nowakowski told Game Developer.

"You come to the studio, you launch Witcher 4 right now," Nowakowski said. "You can launch it on PC. You can launch it on PS5. You can launch it on Xbox Series X, and it's going to run."

That's in contrast to how Cyberpunk 2077 worked its way through development—the whole thing was PC-driven, Nowakowski said. "The way the studio was thinking was that we are reaching for the best possible visuals," he said. "We want to push the boundaries of what is doable in terms of cinematic feeling and whatnot, and PC was just the best suited rig for that. There was this, as it turned out, false belief that toning it down to whatever was the current gen is not going to be that much of a challenge."

Related: Opinion: Deprofessionalization could foster toxic work environments on small teams

Nowakowski said CD Projekt Red faced this sort of challenge with The Witcher 3 , but "got a bit lucky here and there," which made the studio feel like Cyberpunk 2077 would end up fine, too. "Since then, we don't take chances," he said. "We want to be sure that it actually works."

If something's wrong with The Witcher 4 on a single platform, the developer stops to fix everything until they're sure of the problem. It means the milestone process for the game is a little different. "For example, technically, we should hit, let's say, 10 checkmarks," he posited. "Back in the past, if we missed one or two, we were like, 'we're gonna catch up with that later on.' Sometimes we did, but sometimes we didn't, and then two milestones or three milestones down the road, you have like four or five missing checkmarks and it's not that easy."

Speaking about the newly announced The Witcher 3 expansion and remaster, Nowakowski said CD Projekt Red is working with a company called Geeksoft, based in Hungary, because of their extensive knowledge of The Witcher 3 's engine—Red Engine. Nowakowski said that the Red Engine used for Cyberpunk 2077 is not the same as it was when used for The Witcher 3 , and revisiting that can be challenging. Geeksoft comes from the modding community, and have "been very active in the world of the Witcher," he said. The company hired them to help with The Witcher 3 's modding tools release. It made sense for them to sign back on for CD Projekt Red's return to that world.

Nowakowski didn't want to give much detail on the future for CD Projekt Red, but said the company will share more about the mysterious Project Hadar "at some point," perhaps, in the next five years. For now, it's back to the task at hand: The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4 .

items.content:
To survive in Night City, you need someone to watch your back. On the way to the major leagues, V managed to gather a remarkable crew. You could even say, a crew to remember!

From trusted allies to unforgettable personalities, these are the people who helped shape V’s journey through the City of Dreams. This episode of It’s All About You is dedicated to the legendary crew that stood by V through every high and low.

Thank you for staying with us and expressing your love for Cyberpunk 2077 in the most creative ways possible. Don’t forget to check out our gallery to see more works, and, of course, share your creations with us: http://cdpred.ly/AAY

See you in the next episode!

items.content:
Listen up, Samurai! 🤘🔥

Celebrate five years of Cyberpunk 2077 in this special anniversary episode of It’s All About You, looking back on Night City’s unforgettable stories through the legends and music you met along your journey!

Sure, the city’s full of noise — sirens, synths, gunfire in the distance — but if there’s one song that became its soul, it’s “Never Fade Away.”

We brought together legendary artists from across the city of dreams to reinterpret this iconic track — each in their own voice, their own style, their own rebellion. ❤️‍🔥

Plug in, turn it up, and dive into our latest It’s All About You episode.

Because legends don’t fade.

items.title: Patch 2.31
items.summary: Patch 2.31 for Cyberpunk 2077 is now live! This update includes an AutoDrive upgrade and Photo Mode adjustments. It also addresses common issues encountered by players. For details, check the full list of changes below: Vehicles Updated Aut
items.content:
Patch 2.31 for Cyberpunk 2077 is now live!

This update includes an AutoDrive upgrade and Photo Mode adjustments. It also addresses common issues encountered by players. For details, check the full list of changes below:

Vehicles

  • Updated AutoDrive. When driving to a selected point, the vehicle now drives smoothly, overtakes blocking vehicles and no longer stops at traffic lights. Free Roam mode has also been upgraded to follow traffic rules and navigate the city more reliably.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Johnny always spawned in the passenger seat when using the Delamain Cab service.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where applying CrystalCoat to the Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru caused its wheels to flash in different colors.

    [/*]

Photo Mode

  • Most of the new poses introduced in Update 2.3 now work with any gender.

    [/*]

  • Disabled NPC collision, which will make it easier to position NPCs on top of other objects with collision (e.g. on car hoods).

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where some of the poses didn't work for Royce.

    [/*]

Quests & Open World

  • Freedom - Fixed the journal entry that appears when the player chooses not to steal the Rayfield Caliburn "Mordred."

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Fixed an issue where, after V fails to pursue and stop Semimaru and receives a text from River saying he'll contact V soon, the follow-up message never arrives.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Fixed an issue where the Yaiba Semimaru could flip over during the chase, preventing the player from entering it.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - It's no longer possible to trigger the quest if River died during The Hunt.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Players can now acquire the Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru through AUTOFIXER even if they failed The Hunt, which normally unlocks the side quest where the vehicle is obtained.

    [/*]

  • Nitro (Youth Energy) - Fixed a game crash that could occur in certain circumstances after leaving the Yaiba showroom event.

    [/*]

  • Nitro (Youth Energy) - Fixed an issue where the proxy interface UI in the Yaiba showroom is cut off when the "Larger HUD Elements" setting is enabled.

    [/*]

Miscellaneous

  • Fixed several localization and lipsync issues in various languages.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle to disable vignette. It can be found in Settings → Graphics → Basic.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on PC and Mac where Ray-Traced Reflections might not display correctly when enabled under certain conditions.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several issues with displaying text messages from Delamain.

    [/*]

  • Various fixes for fluff vendors.

    [/*]

PC-specific

  • Fixed an issue where NVIDIA Reflex could be disabled while DLSS Frame Generation was enabled, causing the screen to turn pink.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Path Tracing didn't activate properly in certain scenarios.

    [/*]

Mac-specific

  • Fixed an issue where changing graphics presets on Mac set Screen Space Reflections to a higher setting compared to the equivalent presets on PC.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue causing a permanent white screen when Frame Generation is enabled while entering the braindance in The Information.

    [/*]

  • Selecting "Defaults" in Video Settings no longer turns HDR Mode off.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where setting the MetalFX DRS Maximum Resolution above the value applied by the “For this Mac” preset could cause visual artifacts.

    [/*]

  • Fixed the inverted behavior of the "Mute Game in Background" toggle in Settings.

    [/*]

  • Removed the outdated "(Requires Game Restart)" disclaimer from the mouseover description of the "Disable Spatial Audio" setting.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on the App Store version that caused the game to become stuck on the “Press Space to continue” breaching screen.

    [/*]

  • Various stability and performance optimizations.

    [/*]

items.title: Update 2.3 Patch Notes
items.summary: Update 2.3 lands tomorrow! Experience Night City in a whole new way — this patch introduces 4 new vehicles, the AutoDrive feature, self-driving Delamain cabs and more! It also contains updates for CrystalCoat™ and Photo Mode, as well as sup
items.content:
Update 2.3 lands tomorrow!

Experience Night City in a whole new way — this patch introduces 4 new vehicles, the AutoDrive feature, self-driving Delamain cabs and more! It also contains updates for CrystalCoat™ and Photo Mode, as well as support for AMD FSR 3.1 Frame Generation, Intel XeSS 2.0 and HDR10+ Gaming, among others.

Update 2.3 also brings Cyberpunk 2077 to a whole new platform: Mac with Apple silicon! If you already own the game on Steam, you can play it on your compatible device. To find out whether your Mac can run Cyberpunk 2077, please check the official requirements.

Read the list of changes for more info:

Vehicles

  • Added 4 new vehicles, including several Side Jobs tied to acquiring them:

    • Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, complete The Hunt and The Beast In Me).

      An additional side job unlocks the CrystalCoat™ feature for it.

      [/*]

    • Rayfield Caliburn "Mordred"

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, complete The Beast in Me: Badlands, The Beast in Me: Santo Domingo, Transmission, and Search and Destroy)."

      [/*]

    • Yaiba ASM-R250 Muramasa

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, purchase 1 Yaiba vehicle, purchase at least 3 vehicles through AUTOFIXER, and complete Reported Crime: You Play with Fire...).

      If you fail the side job, the vehicle can later be purchased through AUTOFIXER.

      [/*]

    • Chevillon Legatus 450 Aquila

      Available for purchase on AUTOFIXER.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Introducing AutoDrive! This cutting-edge, autonomous driving feature will take you to your chosen destination (i.e. job objective or placed pin on the map). If you have no set destination, it will take you on a leisurely ride through the streets of Night City. Simply hop in any of your vehicles, make sure you're on a road, and hold G (PC) / Left Stick (consoles) to activate. This feature is disabled when you enter combat or when your vehicle is heavily damaged.

    [/*]

  • Implemented Cinematic Camera for AutoDrive. Hold Q (PC) / D-Pad Right (consoles) to activate. Sit back and enjoy cinematic views of Night City as you cruise toward your destination.

    [/*]

  • Self-driving Delamain cabs are now available on demand! Simply open the menu to call vehicles, then select "Delamain Cab" from the list to request a ride. This feature unlocks after completing the job Don't Lose Your Mind (regardless of outcome) and receiving a message from Delamain.

    [/*]

  • Rayfield's CrystalCoat™ is now available for vehicles from partner brands, including motorcycles. Additionally, the infamous hacker known as Cosmetic_Troll exploited a vulnerability and created a cracked version of Rayfield's CrystalCoat™ technology for lower-end vehicles. Please note, however, that some models do not support the technology, such as heavily modded nomad vehicles and job-related vehicles.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where unique color schemes did not work properly on the Mizutani Shion MZ1 and MZ2.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where unique color scheme could not be applied properly to the Villefort Deleon "Vindicator".

    [/*]

Photo Mode

  • Added 27 new NPCs that can be spawned in Photo Mode, including Rita Wheeler, the Cassel twins, fixers, Dum Dum, the iguana, Brendan, and more.

    [/*]

  • You can now switch between alternative outfits for NPCs spawned in Photo Mode.

    [/*]

  • You can now switch between V's saved Wardrobe outfits in Photo Mode.

    [/*]

  • Added a confirmation pop-up when exiting Photo Mode to prevent accidental exits after setting up the perfect shot.

    [/*]

  • Added more customization options to the Look-At Camera feature, including an option for only the character's eyes to turn toward the camera instead of their entire body.

    [/*]

  • Added improvements to Lighting:

    • Lights now spawn around the camera instead of the player character.

      [/*]

    • Added an outline to the spotlight mesh and an indicator when it's off screen for better visibility.

      [/*]

    • Improved light movement speed on controllers.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Added multiple new stickers and frames, including iconic quotes and stylish overlays that let you turn your screenshots into Night City postcards – perfect for sharing memories from the City of Dreams.

    [/*]

  • Improved Depth of Field and moved it to the Camera tab.

    [/*]

  • Added a new Color Balance tab, allowing you to create your own custom filters.

    [/*]

  • Added a new Time and Weather tab:

    • Weather: includes rain, acid rain, fog, sandstorm, pollution, and sunny.

      [/*]

    • Time of Day: changes the time of day within Photo Mode.

      [/*]

    • Frame Forward: advances through an unlimited amount of frames to capture the perfect shot.

      [/*]

    • Game Speed: allows in-game time to progress while in Photo Mode."

      [/*]
    [/*]

Quality of Life & Accessibility

  • The game will now detect if the player is using inverted mouse button settings and automatically adjusts in-game button prompts accordingly.

    [/*]

  • Added an option to toggle aiming down sights in Settings → Controls.

    [/*]

Jobs & Open World

  • Cyberpsycho Sighting: Bloody Ritual - the "Crack the ritualist's shard" objective now properly disappears from the Journal after completing the objective.

    [/*]

  • Sex on Wheels - now properly appears in the Journal after receiving the message from Jake Estevez.

    [/*]

  • Shot by Both Sides - fixed an issue where selecting a specific dialogue option in the conversation with Bree created a nameless, iconless item in the player's Inventory.

    [/*]

  • Shot by Both Sides - fixed an issue where the button to go to the lower level didn't appear on the elevator panel.

    [/*]

Gameplay

  • Fixed an issue where, when using a controller in Trauma Drama, the controllable character would default to shooting upwards instead of forward.

    [/*]

  • Players can now drop more Cyberware Capacity Shards if some within the intended drop limit were previously missed.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue causing automatic weapons to fire slower than intended.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the Official BARGHEST Tac Vest didn't drop from the scripted Airdrop as intended.

    [/*]

  • The level 60 Engineer perk no longer activates the EMP blast outside of combat or after entering a vehicle.

    [/*]

  • Added an option to replay the gameplay tutorial at any time via Settings → Controls.

    [/*]

Miscellaneous

  • Added an option to tell Johnny to go away after you look at him for a short while when he appears in the passenger seat. He takes the hint and disappears as a passenger for a couple days.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the sound of V's Radioport could be randomly interrupted by the Radioports of nearby NPCs.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where History by Gazelle Twin and Trash Generation played too loudly compared to other songs on the radio.

    [/*]

  • Improved the HDR Setting screen: fixed the HDR calibration preview so it correctly reflects the chosen settings, and clarified the description of the "Tone-Mapping Midpoint" setting.

    [/*]

  • Updated the End User Licence Agreement. You will be asked to accept it again when you load the game after updating.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several visual issues with missing, clipping, or floating textures.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several localization issues in various languages.

    [/*]

PC-specific

  • Added support for AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 4 for compatible AMD GPUs. IMPORTANT: The FSR 4 option will not be available in the in-game settings until the supporting AMD driver is installed. Please note that the driver will be released at a later date.

    [/*]

  • Added support for AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution Frame Generation 3.1 for compatible hardware. It can now be used in combination with any upscaler.

    [/*]

  • Added support for ​Intel XeSS 2.0, with XeSS Frame Generation available on compatible hardware.

    [/*]

  • Added support for HDR10+ GAMING certified Intel GPUs. To enable this feature, your display must support the technology (find my display) and have "Game Mode" enabled. The HDR10+ GAMING toggle can be found in Settings in the Video tab.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the DLSS Super Resolution Preset would invisibly revert from the CNN model to the Transformer model after restarting the game, even though the UI still displayed the CNN model as active.

    [/*]

  • Added more detailed information to the DLSS Super Resolution Preset tooltip in Settings to help players choose the best option for their setup.

    [/*]

  • Added the ability to move the mouse cursor to a different display while in Windowed Borderless mode.

    [/*]

  • Increased the maximum save size from 12 MB to 15 MB.

    [/*]

  • It will now be possible to rebind the key used to jump out of vehicles with the Stuntjock perk.

    [/*]
